methodology: Downloaded the NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) 2023 National CSV archive and extracted accident.csv (one row per fatal motor-vehicle crash, national level, calendar year 2023). Read with UTF-8 encoding (verified to also decode cleanly under latin-1, but UTF-8 succeeded so it was used). Selected columns STATENAME, ST_CASE, MONTH, LATITUDE, LONGITUD, FATALS. Rows with unknown/unreported coordinate sentinel codes were dropped: LATITUDE >= 77 (covers the FARS 'unknown' codes 77.7777, 88.8888, 99.9999) or LATITUDE null; LONGITUD with absolute value >= 300 (covers 777.7777, 888.8888, 999.9999) or LONGITUD null; rows where (LATITUDE, LONGITUD) == (0, 0). All remaining valid rows were kept -- every fatal crash of 2023 with usable geocoding, no sampling or aggregation. Coordinates were rounded to 3 decimal places for the staging file. v = FATALS (fatalities in that crash). meta.m = MONTH (1-12).

source.name: NHTSA FARS 2023 National CSV
source.note: 2023 zip returned HTTP 200 on first attempt; no fallback to 2022 was needed.

caveats: 129 of 37,769 crashes (0.34%) had unknown/unreported GPS coordinates (FARS sentinel codes 77.7777/88.8888/99.9999 latitude paired with 777.7777/888.8888/999.9999 longitude) and were dropped from the point layer; no (lat,lon) == (0,0) rows or null coordinates were present in this year's file.

This represents 2023 data (the most recent full annual FARS release at time of retrieval), not the '~39,000' figure mentioned as an estimate in the task -- the actual 2023 total is 37,769 fatal crashes before filtering, 37,640 after filtering, resulting in 41,025 total deaths unfiltered / 40,889 total deaths in the kept records.

FARS accident-level LATITUDE/LONGITUD reflect NHTSA's geocoded crash location; precision varies by state reporting practice and rural roads may be geocoded to a milepost/route reference point rather than the exact crash site.
Coordinates rounded to 3 decimal places (~110m precision) per staging spec; this is a deliberate precision reduction for the map layer, not a data quality issue.
